title: The Ghost in the Graveyard

full_text:
Traveling home late at night after attending a religious discourse in a neighboring town, Guru Paramartha and his five disciples had to pass beside the ancient village cremation ground, where banyan trees cast eerie shadows and white limestone memorial stones gleamed in the moonlight.

The disciples huddled close together, trembling at every rustle of dry leaves.

'Master,' whispered Asadan, his voice shaking, 'this burial ground is inhabited by bloodthirsty ghosts, or Pisachas, who hang upside-down from trees and devour unwary travelers!'

The Guru cleared his throat, trying to sound courageous: 'Fear not, children! A true philosopher is fortified by the sacred mantras of truth. No phantom can harm a man of pure intellect!'

At that moment, a sudden gust of wind whistled through the thorn bushes. Directly in the center of the cremation ground, standing atop a mound of earth, was a tall, white, ghostly figure with outstretched arms, swaying rhythmically in the breeze!

Matti fell to the earth: 'A GHOST! A WHITE DEMON WAITS FOR US!'

The disciples turned to flee, but the Guru held them back with his staff: 'Halt! If we run, the ghost will pursue us and strike us down from behind! We must confront the spirit with philosophical logic!'

'Who will address the phantom?' asked Madayan.

The Guru pushed Peedan forward: 'Peedan, you have the loudest voice; step forward three paces and demand his lineage and purpose!'

Peedan, his knees knocking together, took two trembling steps toward the swaying white figure. In a squeaky, terrified voice, he stammered: 'O... O noble spirit of the burial mound! Are you a ghost of the upper air or a demon of the netherworld? Speak, or our Guru will destroy you with Vedic fire!'

The white figure did not speak; it merely swayed its arms in the wind.

Madayan observed: 'He waves his arms! He is summoning his demonic legions from beneath the earth! We must attack him before his army arrives!'

Guru Paramartha commanded: 'Pick up stones, my valiant disciples! Pelt the demon with all your might!'

The five disciples and the Guru gathered heavy granite stones from the roadside. Standing in a line, they launched a furious bombardment: THROW! CLATTER! THWACK!

Dozens of stones flew through the air, striking the white figure. With a hollow crack, the demon collapsed to the ground, its white drapery fluttering in the dust.

'VICTORY!' shouted Matti. 'We have slain the ghost!'

Approaching cautiously with their sticks raised, the disciples poked the fallen monster.

To their astonishment, they found that the 'ghost' was nothing more than an old wooden scarecrow constructed of two crossed sticks, draped in a white cotton bedsheet by the cemetery watchman to frighten stray cattle away from the newly planted jasmine bushes!

Guru Paramartha poked the sheet with his staff and remarked with solemn satisfaction: 'Behold, my children! Even the inanimate scarecrow surrendered before our philosophical bombardment! Let us proceed with victory!'

And the disciples marched home, singing hymns of triumph over the vanquished phantom.
moral: Superstition turns harmless objects into terrifying ghosts; reason dispels the phantoms of the night.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Ghost in the Graveyard"?
options: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
